newsitem.title: USA: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates change little in week.
newsitem.headline: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates change little in week.

text.p: The average commitment rate on U.S. 30-year fixed rate mortgages rose one basis point to 8.16 percent in the week ended April 18 from 8.15 percent last week, while 15-year mortgages inched upward to 7.71 percent from 7.67 percent, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
One-year adjustable rate mortgages dipped to an average 5.89 percent from 5.91 percent, it said.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.95 percent, the 15-year 7.48 percent and the ARM 5.75 percent.
"There was renewed evidence this week that inflation is in check, so we may even see a slight drop in rates next week," Frank Nothaft, Freddie Mac chief economist, said.
"Housing starts remain at relatively high levels, and the spring homebuying season promises to be strong," Nothaft added. "Homebuyers can expect favorable rates for the foreseeable future."

On Wednesday the Commerce Department said U.S. March housing starts fell 6.4 percent to an annualized rate of 1.425 million units, while the Labor Department Tuesday said consumer prices rose by only 0.1 percent last month.
Lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, down from 1.8 percent last week. They charged 1.4 percent on ARM loans, down from 1.5 percent last week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
